notes: Not a real problem, so the graph is unchanged: the [E8] 'needs at least 7.0 V but 3V3 is on 3.3 V' warning treats the Due's 3V3 pin as a supply input. On the Arduino Due, 3V3 is an output from the board's on-board 3.3 V regulator. The tutorial and its image use it to feed the breadboard 3.3 V rail through a red wire, which powers the potentiometer and the button supply sides. Nothing powers the Due from that pin.

The Due itself is powered through its USB or power-jack input, with 7-12 V or 5 V USB. The tutorial lists no power source or USB cable, so I added none. This matches the manual's exact parts list. Nothing in the circuit drives a 5 V signal into the 3.3 V-only I/O pins.
Used arduino-due-r3 because the circuit needs D2, D3 and A0. The 'arduino-due' card lists only power ports. I assumed arduino-due-r3 also has ports named 3V3 and GND.
Rails: tp and bp are 3.3 V, tn and bn are ground. wire3 and wire4 join the top rails to the bottom rails.
Potentiometer: one outer leg to 3.3 V, the other outer leg to ground, wiper to A0 (yellow wire). It sits in columns 14-16 in the order GND, SIG, VCC.

Each pushbutton sits across the centre gap. Side 1 (top half) has the input-pin wire (D2 or D3) and the 10k pull-down resistor to ground on the same side. Side 2 (bottom half) goes to 3.3 V. The two legs of a side are joined inside the button, so one wire per side is enough.
The image places the resistors and red wires near the bottom of the breadboard. I followed the circuit text, so exact hole positions are my own choice.
Every physical connection has a joined edge and an electrical edge between the same ports.
